chapter: Chicago in the 1920s: Bix, Armstrong, Morton
title: Sitting in with Bix Beiderbecke and Muggsy at the Paradise Inn
summary: Howard played one night at the tiny Paradise Inn at 35th and Prairie with Bix and Muggsy sitting in.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Did you ever see Big Spider back?
Sure, I played with him in Chicago. At the place called Paradise Inn, on the very fitting prairie.

He didn't work with them, he set in with us. Him and Muggsy. Oh yeah? Yeah, him and Muggsy. You mean they came in together? Yes. Who were you working with? Oh, just a little patched up band, wasn't any name band. We were just playing in this place. I'm trying to get a man named him in that place. There was about five of us. Paradise Inn, let's call it. 35th and Prairie.
Yeah, right on the corner. Wasn't very big. Put you in mind the timpani about that size.
Yeah, a club like that. It wasn't too big. Yes. And we had to play soft. Oh yeah?

The doors was wide open in the summertime. Bass Shade played, when they playing Clannaddy, you could hear him down 31st Street, five blocks off. I'm not lying to you. Because they had the windows open, you know. Yeah.
Was Bix playing good at that time? Oh, heck yes.

He was on his way to New York then. Was he pretty well known then? Did musicians know about him? Well, my musicians may have known him, but… Not the club? No. Man, I loved his playing. Is that the only time you played with him? Yeah. Just once, huh? That's right. He came in there again, but that night he didn't play with us.
He came in a couple of times. Mm-hmm.
